# Security

Everything shipped in the bundle is public: front-end security is about never putting there what must stay secret.

Marker after the identifier: a tool name = tooled constraint (the build or the commit fails); `guidance` = rule of conduct checked in review.

## Base rules

### Rules

- **CORE-070** · `gitleaks` — Everything shipped in the bundle is public; no secret, key or private token is ever read by the browser code.
  Why: A `VITE_` variable is inlined at build time and readable by anyone who opens the sources.
- **CORE-071** · `gitleaks` — `.env.example` is committed with every expected variable; `.env` is ignored and never committed.
  Why: A new developer must be able to start the project without asking which variables exist.
- **CORE-072** · `eslint` — `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is used only on content sanitised by the dedicated module of `shared/`.
  Why: Any other use turns a stored string into script execution.
- **CORE-073** · `eslint` — A link opened in a new tab carries `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
  Why: Without it the opened page can drive the tab it came from.
- **CORE-074** · guidance — An authentication token is never written to `localStorage` or `sessionStorage`.
  Why: Any injected script reads them; a cookie set by the server does not have that weakness.
- **CORE-075** · guidance — A Content-Security-Policy is served in production and the application ships no inline script.
  Why: The policy is the last barrier when an injection gets through.
- **CORE-076** · guidance — User input interpolated into a URL is encoded, and a URL coming from data is never used as a `src` or `href` without checking its scheme.
  Why: A `javascript:` URL stored in a field is executed on click.
- **CORE-077** · guidance — Dependencies are audited in CI, and adding one is a separate commit stating why it is needed.
  Why: The front-end dependency tree is the widest attack surface of the project.

### Anti-patterns

- **CORE-AP-070** · `gitleaks` — Putting an API key in a `VITE_` variable and treating it as private.
  Why: The value ends up in the JavaScript bundle, in clear text.
  Instead: Keep the key on a server and call it through the project's backend.

## Option `security-none`

No authentication in the interface; the API is reached directly.

### Rules

- **SECN-001** · guidance — No route is hidden behind a client-side check that pretends to protect it.
  Why: A check the browser performs protects nothing; it only misleads the next reader.
- **SECN-002** · guidance — No authentication dependency is added without changing this choice in `scaffold.yaml` first.
  Why: Authentication added on the side, screen by screen, is how a hole is left open.
